title: A batch left out of the reveal
story: The client's metadata reveal stops one batch short. It leaves out the last batch the server stored for the re-score range, which holds A3's stop at 19:46:00 and the presence sample taken with it. Every batch it reveals reproduces, and b and seq rise with no gap, so only the server's own rows show what is missing.
edits: The transcript's user entry for each prompt, read by the log reader 0.7 to 4.5 s after the hook (via log, same turn_key and lengths), as a real Claude Code client records it.
The reveal has no batch 3030, the last one the server stored for the re-score range: A3's agent.stop at 19:46:00 and its presence sample. events.jsonl keeps both, as the client recorded them.

CC6.basis: Stated, not recomputed: the server's re-score lacks A3's stop and the 19:46:00 sample, which bear only on 19:45: the sample closes its last slot, and the stop ends a turn that 19:45 discounts as X.reroll. CC7 holds 19:45, and every other minute of W depends only on revealed records, so it reproduces.

CC10.reason: no editor act in the submission

notes: A reveal that drops batches at either end of the range shows no gap in b or seq and nothing that fails to reproduce. Only the server's rows for the re-score range, 19:16 to 20:01, show that a batch is missing (DESIGN 7.5 step 3).

The missing batch's records lie between the last verified record, A3's answer at 19:45:58, and the time the server received the batch, 19:46:01, so CC7 holds 19:45 and 19:46. Only 19:45 is in W, and it credits nothing: A3 is the third A.
The other checks read records in W, and the missing batch has none: its two records are at 19:46:00, where W ends.
The missing batch reveals no record, so CC7 holds no other minute.
